text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Parties and armed forces critise Islamist MP who, in a television interview, revealed plans for Islamists to infiltrate military academies.
- Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan says Turkey will not go and beg for full membership of the European Union.

- Former prime minister Mesut Yilmaz gives the president documents collected during his three-month-long premiership, which he said could serve as proof in an investigation into alleged ties between organised crime, police and the state.
- The Welfare Party, the Islamist wing of the government, is pushing through a human rights package for the lifting of a ban on civil sevants wearing Islamist headscarves and sporting beards.
- Coalition partner at fight over opening land route for those going on Moslem pilgrimage to Mecca.
- Women wearing the Islamist viel entered parliament to attend a meeting of Welfare Party deputies, violating the parliament's dress code.
- MPs vote to accept an opposition-led motion for a parliamentary investigation into alleged state-mafia links.
- The Turkish Grain Board (TMO) begins selling wheat to local millers in a government attempt to curb a rise in bread prices.
- Three killed in a Turkish military helicopter crash near the eastern Greek island of Rhodes.
